h1: Landscaping & lawn care in White Oak
lede: White Oak sits right next door to our Longview home base. We mow, plant and build here with the same crew every time, and the estimate is free and in writing.
intro: Yard Dog Landscapes handles landscaping and lawn care in White Oak, TX from our home base just east in Longview. We're family-owned, started in 2017 by Miller Maines, and Miller and the same crew of four do the work every time, never a subcontractor. We're fully insured and rated 5.0 on Google from {{REVIEWS}} reviews. Request a free walkthrough anytime and get a written, itemized estimate, usually within a day.

White Oak is a small Gregg County town strung along US 80 between Longview and Gladewater. A lot of the yards in town are established lots under mature trees, with St. Augustine in the shade and Bermuda wherever the sun gets through. The ground runs sandy and drains well, which is good for roots and hard on anything that needs steady water. Outside town the lots get bigger, and so do the projects.

This year we built two of those bigger projects in White Oak: a raised boat and RV pad held by a pressure-treated timber wall, and a 475 square foot Cherokee flagstone patio built around a chopped stone fire pit. Being this close to the shop means we can walk a White Oak yard without a long haul and get back out quickly after a storm to check our work. Between the bigger builds, we handle the everyday work here too: mowing, hedges, leaf cleanup and bed refreshes.

yard_notes.title: Shade from established trees
yard_notes.text: Many in-town White Oak lots sit under mature oaks and pines. Grass thins where the canopy closes in and hedges stretch toward the light, so shade decides most of what we recommend here.

yard_notes.title: Sandy ground that drains fast
yard_notes.text: White Oak soil runs sandy. New sod and beds root easily but dry out quickly, so watering and mulch matter more here than on heavier ground.

yard_notes.title: Room for bigger builds
yard_notes.text: Larger lots around town leave room for pads, patios and fire pits. Where the ground falls away, we build the grade up with a wall instead of setting stone on a slope.

yard_notes.title: Downspouts and flat spots
yard_notes.text: Even sandy yards hold water where downspouts dump at the foundation or the lot runs flat. A short drain run or a regrade usually solves it.

faq.q: Do you serve all of White Oak?
faq.a: Yes. We work in town and on the larger lots around it, and White Oak is just a short drive west of our Longview base on US 80. If you're out between White Oak and Gladewater and not sure you're in range, send a quote request and we'll confirm.

faq.q: What went into the boat and RV pad you built in White Oak?
faq.a: We raised a level pad for parking a boat and RV, held the fill in place with a pressure-treated timber wall, laid drainage fabric and topped it with gravel. The fabric keeps the gravel from working down into the soil, and rain drains through the pad instead of pooling on it.

faq.q: How much does a patio or retaining wall cost in White Oak?
faq.a: Most patio and hardscape projects run $3,100 to $9,100, and most retaining walls run $3,000 to $19,000 depending on height and length. Size, stone choice and how much the ground has to be built up move the number. You get the exact price in writing after we walk the yard.

faq.q: Do you only build projects in White Oak, or do you mow too?
faq.a: Both. We mow, trim hedges and clean up leaves in White Oak, along with building patios, walls and drainage. Weekly mowing starts at $65 per visit for a typical yard, and larger lots are priced after a walkthrough.

service_angles.lawn-maintenance: White Oak yards tend to be established lots where shade and sun split the lawn in two. We mow the St. Augustine under the trees taller and the Bermuda in the open shorter, trim around trunks and beds, and keep the cut high in summer so the sandy ground doesn't bake the roots. Typical yards start at $65 per visit.
service_angles.leaf-removal: Mature trees over many White Oak properties mean a heavy fall drop, and on bigger properties the leaves pile up along fences and in back corners where nobody looks until spring. We clear lawns, beds and drives and haul it all off. Leaf removal is quoted after we walk the property, since tree cover and lot size set the job.
service_angles.fertilization: White Oak's sandy soil lets nutrients wash through faster than they would on clay. We lean on slower-release feedings timed to the season and a fall winterizer heavy in potassium, and we soil test to see if the ground needs lime. Feeding visits start from about $190.
service_angles.hedge-trimming: Hedges under White Oak's shade trees grow leggy and thin at the bottom as they reach for light. We shape them slightly narrower at the top than the base so sun reaches the lower branches, and keep foundation shrubs off the brick and out of the windows. Most hedge jobs run $150 to $800.
service_angles.tree-shrub-care: On established White Oak lots the work is often catch-up: shrubs that outgrew their beds, crepe myrtles cut wrong for years, low limbs dragging on a shed roof or shading out the grass. We prune by species and season, take out small trees and shrubs that have run their course and haul everything off. It's quoted after a walkthrough.
service_angles.tree-planting: White Oak's sandy loam is easy to dig and drains well, so a new tree here lives or dies on water through its first two summers. When we can, we plant between September and Thanksgiving, set the root ball at the right height, build a basin and mulch ring and leave you a watering schedule. We quote tree planting after seeing the spot.
service_angles.sod-installation: Sod takes quickly in White Oak's sandy ground, and it dries out just as quickly. We match the grass to the light, St. Augustine where trees shade the lot and Bermuda in full sun, then level the base and set a watering plan that keeps the roots damp until they knit. Sod is priced by the pallet, and most jobs land between $1,500 and $4,700.
service_angles.landscaping: A lot of White Oak landscaping starts with a yard that has good bones and tired beds. We rework the bed lines, amend the sandy soil with compost and plant shade-tolerant shrubs and perennials where the trees cast their shadow, and bigger lots often pair the planting with a patio or fire pit. Most planting projects run $900 to $3,600.
service_angles.flower-bed-installation: White Oak's sandy beds drain well but run low on nutrients and dry fast, and many sit in dappled shade. We work in compost before anything goes in, then pick plants that bloom on a half day of sun instead of fighting for it. A fresh layer of mulch finishes each bed to hold the water in.
service_angles.mulch-installation: On White Oak's sandy beds, mulch does the work of holding moisture that the soil can't hold on its own. We clean the beds, re-cut the edges and spread an even layer, pulled back off trunks and the foundation. Most refreshes run $600 to $2,400, and pine straw is an option if you like the look under the pines.
service_angles.hardscaping: Our 475 square foot Cherokee flagstone patio in White Oak shows how we build here: chopped stone edging, mortared joints and a chopped stone fire pit, with one corner raised on a chopped stone wall where the ground fell away. Every patio starts on a dug-out, compacted base. Most patios we build run $3,100 to $9,100.
service_angles.retaining-walls: In White Oak we built a pressure-treated timber wall to hold the fill under a raised boat and RV pad, with drainage fabric and gravel so water passes through instead of building up. Block and stone walls follow the same rule on the sandy ground here: a compacted base, gravel backfill and somewhere for the water to go. Most walls run $3,000 to $19,000.
service_angles.drainage: Sandy soil in White Oak drains well on its own, so most problems come from downspouts dumping at the foundation or flat spots where water has nowhere to run. We fix those with downspout extensions, short drain runs, swales and pop-up emitters. Small fixes start around $450, and most full projects run $2,000 to $3,750.
service_angles.christmas-lights: White Oak is a short drive from our shop, well inside our normal install range. We supply the lights, custom-cut professional C9 lines to your roofline, put them up, take them down after the season and store them until next year. Quotes come from a photo mock-up of your house, and most homes start at $900.
service_angles.irrigation: White Oak's sandy soil drinks water fast and dries out fast, so coverage has to be even or the lawn browns in strips by July. We space heads for full overlap, split sun and shade into their own zones, and put the beds on drip so the roots get the water instead of the siding.

lawn-maintenance.q: Does White Oak's sandy soil change how you mow?
lawn-maintenance.a: It changes the height. Sandy ground dries out fast, so we leave the grass taller through summer, around three and a half to four inches for St. Augustine. Taller grass shades the soil and roots deeper, which helps the lawn ride out dry stretches.

leaf-removal.q: Do you clear leaves from large White Oak lots?
leaf-removal.a: Yes. Bigger properties with a lot of trees are quoted after a walkthrough, and some need a second pass in December after the oaks finish dropping. We haul everything off rather than leaving piles at the curb.

fertilization.q: How often should a White Oak lawn be fertilized?
fertilization.a: Most lawns do well on four feedings: late April once nights warm up, early July, early September and a potassium-heavy winterizer in October. Sandy soil lets nutrients wash through, so smaller, well-timed feedings beat one heavy one.

hedge-trimming.q: Can you bring back overgrown hedges in White Oak?
hedge-trimming.a: Usually. Most overgrown shrubs can take a harder rejuvenation cut in late winter and fill back in by summer. Some, like old boxwoods, come back slowly, and a few are better replaced. We'll tell you which is which on the walkthrough.

tree-shrub-care.q: Do you remove trees in White Oak?
tree-shrub-care.a: We remove small trees and shrubs. Large trees, especially near a house or power lines, are a job for a tree service with the right equipment. We handle pruning, shaping and cleanup on everything we can safely reach.

tree-planting.q: When should I plant a tree in White Oak?
tree-planting.a: Fall is the best window, from September until around Thanksgiving. The soil stays warm enough for roots to grow while the air cools, so the tree has months to settle in before summer. Spring planting works, but it takes a lot more water to get a young tree through its first August.

sod-installation.q: How much water does new sod need in White Oak?
sod-installation.a: More than most people expect, because sandy ground dries out fast. Plan on keeping new sod damp every day for the first couple of weeks, then backing off as the roots take hold. We leave a watering plan with every install.

landscaping.q: Can you landscape a shady White Oak yard?
landscaping.a: Yes. Shade is common here, and we plan around it with shade-tolerant shrubs, ferns and ground covers, plus mulch or stone where grass won't grow. Forcing sun plants under big trees is a mistake we see a lot.

flower-bed-installation.q: What grows in shady White Oak flower beds?
flower-bed-installation.a: Azaleas, hydrangeas, cast iron plant, holly ferns and caladiums all do well in part shade here. We set them in amended soil and mulch them so they're not fighting the sand for water.

mulch-installation.q: How deep should mulch be on White Oak beds?
mulch-installation.a: About 1 to 1.5 inches over a prepped bed. Pile it thicker and it sheds light rain like a tarp, leaving the sandy soil underneath dry while the mulch itself stays damp against the stems. We loosen the top of the soil first so water gets through, then top up to that depth instead of piling new on old.

hardscaping.q: Do you build fire pits in White Oak?
hardscaping.a: Yes. Our White Oak flagstone patio was built around a chopped stone fire pit, with chopped stone edging to match. Fire pits sit on a compacted base so they stay level as the ground around them settles.

retaining-walls.q: Is a timber retaining wall a good choice in White Oak?
retaining-walls.a: For the right job, yes. We used pressure-treated timber for the wall under a raised boat and RV pad in White Oak, where it holds fill and gravel on a working pad. For walls near the house or in the main yard, block or stone usually lasts longer and looks more finished.

drainage.q: Why does my White Oak yard hold water if the soil is sandy?
drainage.a: Sandy topsoil usually sits on a firmer layer below, and once the top saturates, water spreads sideways. Downspouts that dump at the foundation and flat spots with no fall make it worse. We find where it collects and give it a path out.

christmas-lights.q: Do you install Christmas lights in White Oak?
christmas-lights.a: Yes. White Oak is close to our Longview base, so it's well within range. Most homes start at $900, and we quote from a photo mock-up of the house, so you can see the layout before you book.

irrigation.q: Do you install sprinkler systems in White Oak?
irrigation.a: Yes. We install and repair sprinkler systems across White Oak under Texas Licensed Irrigator Matthew Maines, LI0006657, and pull whatever permit the job requires. It's a short drive from Longview, and the walkthrough and quote are free.
